messages:
alex: Heads-up — over the last 20m we've seen a sudden spike of TCP resets and 5xxs hitting model pulls from edge pods in eu-west-1. Affected: inference-prep jobs and some cold-starts. Errors show ECONNRESET and handshake timeouts.

maria: yikes. any correlation with deploys or autoscaler events?

alex: No deploys. CPU/GPU fine. Network metrics show outbound connection churn and NAT gateway connection count near the soft limit. NAT metrics: active connections ~= 62k, ephemeral ports approaching 64k.

jamal: that sounds like ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT side. Are we multiplexing model pulls over long-lived connections?

alex: not reliably. Each model pull currently creates a bunch of short-lived connections to s3/model-registry. clients use default keepalive TTLs.

tara: quick triage ideas: 1) force reuse/keepalive on model fetch clients, 2) route model pulls through our egress proxy that supports connection pooling, 3) add s3 VPC endpoint to avoid NAT, 4) temporary NAT gateway scale request with cloud provider.

maria: Also look at TCP TIME_WAIT buildup on node side. If kernels are in TIME_WAIT, can reduce TIME_WAIT by enabling tcp_tw_reuse/tcp_tw_recycle? (careful) Alternative: increase ephemeral port range.

jamal: note: tcp_tw_recycle is dangerous with NAT, don't enable. Prefer tcp_tw_reuse=1 and lower TIME_WAIT with proper keepalives. And increase ip_local_port_range to widen ephemeral pool.

alex: here's a short snippet from the edge proxy logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T08:12:01Z] http: client -> 10.3.5.12: outbound connect error: dial tcp: lookup s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com: no route to host; cause: connection reset after 4096 open sockets
```

tara: actionable checklist I propose: 
- short: flip model fetch to use VPC S3 endpoint for eu-west-1 (no NAT)
- short: patch model-fetch client to enable keepalive + HTTP/2 multiplexing (reuse sockets)
- short: route critical model pulls to reserved egress IP pool with dedicated NATs
- medium: open cloud ticket for NAT capacity increase + autoscale policy review
- med/long: deploy lightweight egress-proxy sidecars to handle pooling for bursty bursts

maria: I can do the VPC endpoint rollout for the staging AZs now and validate. Jamal, can you prepare a config change for the model fetcher to set KeepAlive=60s and MaxIdleConnsPerHost=100?

jamal: on it. I'll push a small client config and a canary. Also adding exponential backoff on retries and jitter so we don't thundering herd.

alex: deploy-bot rolled back inference-prep job 2026-03-18_08:15:23 due to repeated pull failures :disappointed:

deploy-bot: Automatic rollback triggered: inference-prep failed 5x within 5m. See job 7821 for logs.

tara: while mari rolls out the endpoint, I'll spin up two temporary NAT gateways in the affected AZ to spread egress. Also lowering node ephemeral port recycle by widening ip_local_port_range. Commands: 
```
# widen ephemeral port range
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"
# allow TIME_WAIT reuse (safe option)
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
```

maria: staged VPC endpoint applied to staging clusters. Initial smoke: model fetches now bypass NAT and succeed. Pushing to prod in 10m if no regressions.

jamal: client config PR: set KeepAlive=60s, MaxIdleConnsPerHost=120, http2 enabled, retries 3 with backoff 200-2000ms + jitter. Will canary in one zone.

alex: after temporary NAT add and client change, connection resets drop to baseline. Still need permanent fixes: egress pooling and change model artifact distribution to warm caches on nodes to avoid mass simultaneous pulls.

tara: opening infra ticket INF-2459 to track: "egress starvation -> ephemeral ports exhaustion": owner jamal, due EOD. Steps: probe port usage daily, add egress proxy rollout plan, provider NAT scaling policy review, S3 endpoint default for model fetches.

maria: noted. Also recommend adding alert: NAT active_conn > 80% for 5m in eu-west-1 with pager.

alex: thanks team. summary: mitigations applied (temporary NAT, VPC endpoint in staging, client keepalive changes), root cause likely bursty short-lived connections causing ephemeral port exhaustion and NAT connection saturation. Will follow up with postmortem if prod rollout goes smoothly. :thumbsup:
